question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hue and cry

options.text: A loud public protest or outcry
A game of hide and seek

explanation: Hue and cry = शोर-शराबा / ज़ोरदार विरोध। Example: There was a hue and cry over the rise in fuel prices.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Part and parcel
explanation: Part and parcel = अभिन्न अंग। Example: Hard work is part and parcel of success.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Ins and outs

options.text: All the detailed facts about something

explanation: Ins and outs = सारी बारीकियाँ। Example: She knows all the ins and outs of the business.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Wear and tear
explanation: Wear and tear = इस्तेमाल से होने वाली टूट-फूट। Example: The insurance does not cover normal wear and tear.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Odds and ends

options.text: The beginning and end of a story

explanation: Odds and ends = इधर-उधर की छोटी-मोटी चीज़ें। Example: The drawer was full of odds and ends.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Time and again
explanation: Time and again = बार-बार। Example: I have warned you time and again.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A white lie

options.text: A harmless lie told to avoid hurting someone

explanation: A white lie = निर्दोष (छोटा) झूठ। Example: He told a white lie to avoid hurting her feelings.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A blue-eyed boy

options.text: A favourite of someone in authority

explanation: A blue-eyed boy = चहेता, प्रिय व्यक्ति। Example: He is the blue-eyed boy of the manager.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A dog in the manger

options.text: A person who spoils others' enjoyment of what he cannot use himself

explanation: A dog in the manger = जो न खुद ले, न दूसरों को लेने दे। Example: Don't be a dog in the manger; let others use the hall.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A cat's paw

options.text: A person used by another to do unpleasant work

explanation: A cat's paw = दूसरों के हाथ की कठपुतली। Example: The clerk was only a cat's paw of the corrupt officer.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A fair-weather friend

options.text: A friend who is always honest
A friend who stays only in good times
A friend who works in a weather office

explanation: A fair-weather friend = मतलबी दोस्त (सिर्फ़ अच्छे समय का साथी)। Example: He proved a fair-weather friend and vanished when I lost my job.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A rolling stone

options.text: A person who never settles in one place or job

explanation: A rolling stone = अस्थिर स्वभाव का व्यक्ति। Example: He is a rolling stone who has changed ten jobs in five years.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A wet blanket

options.text: A person who spoils others' enjoyment

explanation: A wet blanket = रंग में भंग डालने वाला। Example: Don't be a wet blanket; come and enjoy the party.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A snake in the grass

options.text: A hidden enemy or treacherous friend

explanation: A snake in the grass = छिपा हुआ शत्रु / विश्वासघाती मित्र। Example: Beware of him; he is a snake in the grass.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A wolf in sheep's clothing

options.text: A dangerous person who pretends to be harmless
A weak person among strong ones

explanation: A wolf in sheep's clothing = भेड़ की खाल में भेड़िया। Example: The kind-looking agent was a wolf in sheep's clothing.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A damp squib
explanation: A damp squib = निराशाजनक असफलता, फुस्स हो जाने वाली चीज़। Example: The much-hyped film turned out to be a damp squib.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cut the Gordian knot

options.text: To solve a difficult problem in a bold way

explanation: Cut the Gordian knot = उलझी समस्या को साहसिक तरीके से सुलझाना। Example: The CEO cut the Gordian knot by closing the loss-making unit.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To leave in the lurch

options.text: To leave early from a party

explanation: Leave in the lurch = मुसीबत में अकेला छोड़ देना। Example: His partners left him in the lurch.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make a clean breast of
explanation: Make a clean breast of = सब कुछ साफ़-साफ़ कबूल कर लेना। Example: The boy made a clean breast of his mistake.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pay lip service

options.text: To express support without really acting on it

explanation: Pay lip service = सिर्फ़ ज़ुबानी समर्थन देना। Example: Many leaders pay lip service to women's rights.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To play fast and loose

options.text: To behave in an irresponsible, unreliable way

explanation: Play fast and loose = बेईमानी/लापरवाही से पेश आना। Example: He played fast and loose with other people's money.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take to one's heels
explanation: Take to one's heels = भाग खड़े होना। Example: The thieves took to their heels on seeing the police.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take French leave
explanation: Take French leave = बिना अनुमति ग़ायब हो जाना। Example: He took French leave from office to watch the match.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To the bitter end

options.text: Until the very end, however difficult

explanation: To the bitter end = अंत तक, चाहे कितना भी कठिन हो। Example: They fought to the bitter end.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: At loggerheads
explanation: At loggerheads = गहरे मतभेद में। Example: The two partners are at loggerheads over profits.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hobson's choice
explanation: Hobson's choice = कोई विकल्प न होना (जो मिले वही लेना)। Example: With only one bus available, it was Hobson's choice.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To nip in the bud

options.text: To stop something at an early stage

explanation: Nip in the bud = शुरू में ही रोक देना। Example: The teacher nipped the trouble in the bud.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cry for the moon
explanation: Cry for the moon = असंभव चीज़ की माँग करना। Example: Asking for a free flat is crying for the moon.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make a clean sweep
explanation: Make a clean sweep = सब कुछ जीत लेना। Example: The party made a clean sweep in the election.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pick holes in
explanation: Pick holes in = कमियाँ निकालना। Example: Critics picked holes in the new policy.
